utfall: Ekstra dager i ordinært (usubsidiert) arbeid over sju år, unge menn 15-24 år (16.6 %); forfatterne ber om forsiktig tolkning for unge
sammenligning: lønnstilskudd mot tidligere ledige ikke-deltakere (matching, scenario 1 uten dødvekt)
sitat: While the long-run average treatment effect on unsubsidised employment (according to scenario 1) is 229 days or 16.6% for young men aged 15 to 24 years and 330 days or 33.3% for men in the middle age group (25 to 44 years), it is 408 days or 49.7% for men between 45 and 54 years of age.

utfall: Ekstra dager i ordinært arbeid over sju år, kvinner under 25 år (10.8 %), mot 454 dager for kvinner 45-54 år
sammenligning: lønnstilskudd mot tidligere ledige ikke-deltakere (matching, scenario 1)
sitat: Likewise, female participants aged between 45 and 54 years achieve in comparison to their matched non-treated counterparts an increase in unsubsidised employment of 454 days or 52.3% in the seven years from program entry, which is considerably higher than it is for women in the middle age group (393 days or 35.4%) and those aged below 25 years (141 days or 10.8%).

utfall: Effekt økende med alder: menn 45-54 år 408 dager ekstra ordinært arbeid over sju år (mot 229 for 15-24 år)
sammenligning: lønnstilskudd mot tidligere ledige ikke-deltakere, eldre mot unge
sitat: While the long-run average treatment effect on unsubsidised employment (according to scenario 1) is 229 days or 16.6% for young men aged 15 to 24 years and 330 days or 33.3% for men in the middle age group (25 to 44 years), it is 408 days or 49.7% for men between 45 and 54 years of age.

utfall: Dødvekt: andel subsidierte ansettelser som ville skjedd uten tilskudd, alle aldre; gjengitt fra Eppel mfl. 2011
sitat: According to their analysis, about a half (52.2%) of all subsidised employment relationships would have been created anyway without the subsidy in the sense of either the identical or a similar combination of workers and employers.
